observations.title: File Your Complaint | Investigations Unit at CRPD Malta
observations.summary: The Investigations Unit page is readable in local Chrome. It describes complaints by persons with disabilities and family members under the Equal Opportunities (Persons with Disability) Act, investigations, amicable resolution and possible court action; it gives investigations@crpd.org.mt for that team. This is broad disability-discrimination information under that Act. It does not itself establish an EAA-specific public, company or exemption route, or an actual EAA enforcement case.
observations.next: Access blocker resolved. Retain the other-law scope; establish an explicit EAA remit and reporting purpose before adding this as an EAA route.

observations.title: Legea prevenirii - ANCOM
observations.summary: Local Chrome rendered the page and the expanded Law 232/2022 offences table. Article 27(1)(f) maps breach of Article 13(1) to RON 6,000–12,000; (g) maps Article 13(2)(a)–(d) to RON 7,000–15,000; (h) maps Article 13(3) to RON 6,000–12,000; (i) maps Article 13(2)(e) to RON 7,000–15,000; (j) maps Article 13(2)(f)–(g) to RON 5,000–10,000. These rows concern service providers and cite Article 27(2) for measures. This establishes EAA-related statutory-sanctions guidance on the page, not an imposed fine, full sector-by-sector jurisdiction or a reporting destination. The table label Notificare: nu is not interpreted as removing service-provider notification duties.
observations.next: Access blocker resolved. Compare the offence mapping and measures with current consolidated Law 232/2022 before a sanctions-table amendment. Confirm sector scope separately; public/company/exemption routes and the missing ADR attachment remain unresolved.

observations.title: EUR-Lex - 62024CA0646 - EN - EUR-Lex
observations.summary: The requested notice rendered in English without the previous TodayOJ redirect. OJ C/2026/2861, published 8 June 2026, reproduces the operative part of the 19 March 2026 judgment in C-646/24. It orders the Republic of Bulgaria to pay the Commission a EUR 1,500,000 lump sum for failure to transpose/notify Directive 2019/882, plus costs. This corroborates the recorded Member-State case; it is not a national business fine or proof of payment.
observations.next: Use the English notice to support the existing separately scoped EU-level transposition-enforcement candidate. Do not create a duplicate case or add the sum to national business-penalty ranges.

observations.title: EUR-Lex - 62024CJ0646 - EN - EUR-Lex
observations.summary: The exact EN-interface URL is readable. EUR-Lex explicitly says the document is unavailable in the interface language and displays the French judgment; its available HTML languages are Bulgarian and French. C-646/24, 19 March 2026, ECLI:EU:C:2026:221: paragraph 31 records withdrawal of the periodic-penalty request; paragraph 123 records complete transposition on 11 April 2025 and 1,017 days of failure; paragraph 127 and operative point 2 impose EUR 1,500,000 on the Republic of Bulgaria. This corroborates the earlier French InfoCuria reading, not a new business sanction. Payment remains unverified.
observations.next: Preserve French document language separately from English interface; reuse the existing EU-level case candidate subject to publication review.
